chapter: Players and bands of old New Orleans
title: Piano players of the period
summary: He names Little Willie, Helen Edwards, Emma Barrett and others as the leading jazz pianists.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who were the best piano players in those days? Well...

I'm gonna tell you. You had some good lady piano players. You had some very good men piano players. They had one little fella around here. He's called Little Willie. Played in my band for a long time. Never had a musical lesson in his life. Don't care what key you pick up, he could pick it up.

Little Willie. He lived out on Sedan Street. Little bit of a fella short fella. Man, he could pick up a key like that. And I mean play. Yeah. Well, I don't know how he passed out. But you had women folks like I was telling you. Oh, that Davis, Helen Edwards, Sadie, Ricard's old lady, what died there. He's married wife, Emma. She's still playing. Emma Berry.

You had Steve. You had Walter Deco. All of them was leading around you at that time on piano for jazz. They all was leading. Fran plays piano too. That's right. Yeah. But Fran just mostly chords. He just chords. He never could pick up a melody. See, that's what I tell him first about playing. Well, how I learned how to pick up a melody and play variation along with it, I used to play a three piece job.
